answer.rationale:
The strongest signal is temporal: a release landed 2 hours ago and the write-path p99 has been climbing for 90 minutes, so the release is the leading suspect and rollback is the only candidate that addresses a cause rather than a symptom. memory_b2 effectively rules out regional_failover here — its recorded failure mode is exactly our current condition (writes hot, 40-minute replication gap, two accounts lost writes), and the primary objective forbids losing customer writes. add_capacity (b3) was validated for a pre-provisioned surge, not a mid-incident latency climb, and would not fix a code regression. enable_circuit_breaker (b4) contained an external partner outage; there is no evidence of a failing dependency, so it would shed load without curing anything. route_read_replicas (b5) is the best fallback and is genuinely relevant since it relieved primary write latency, but our load is settlement writes at peak, not dashboard reads, so the mechanism may not transfer.

I want to verify memory_b1 because I am about to reuse it under conditions it may not cover: the day-18 rollback is recorded as clean, but I do not know whether it happened during heavy write traffic or whether the release contained a schema/data-format migration. A rollback across a forward-migrated schema at peak settlement is precisely how a stability action becomes a write-loss action — the failure mode I am trying to avoid by rejecting failover. I want to verify memory_b6 because it partially contradicts my hypothesis: if staged release gating reliably surfaces regressions within an hour of canary, a build that passed gating and only degraded gradually 2 hours later may not be the cause at all, which would redirect me toward b5.

Uncertainty is real: I have correlation, not causation, and three simultaneous conditions any of which could explain the climb. So I intend a small_guarded_test — roll back a limited fraction of the fleet first and compare write-path p99 against the un-rolled-back remainder, rather than a broad rollout that would be hard to reverse mid-peak. If the archive shows b1's rollback was write-quiet or migration-free, or b6 undercuts the release hypothesis, I will hold the rollback for the next window and take route_read_replicas instead.
